- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and prices are trending upward, model often underestimates; adjust up by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overforecasting in next period; apply lag correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast if prior 3-day spike occurred.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above 65.0, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until price stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period corrections; if sentiment turns negative after day 15–20, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for remaining days.
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.6→0.8→0.9), model tends to overforecast; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% for next 3–5 days.
